## PART 2 - PRODUCTS > 2.8 AGGREGATES FOR CONCRETE > TABLE - 10 / GRADING OF FINE AGGREGATES
[IS 383 - Table 4]

| IS Sieve Designation   | Percentage Passing for - Grading Zone I   | Percentage Passing for - Grading Zone II   | Percentage Passing for - Grading Zone III   | Percentage Passing for - Grading Zone IV   |
|------------------------|-------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------|
| 10 mm                  | 100                                       | 100                                        | 100                                         | 100                                        |
| 4.75 mm                | 90 to 100                                 | 90 to 100                                  | 90 to 100                                   | 95 to 100                                  |
| 2.36 mm                | 60 to 95                                  | 75 to 100                                  | 85 to 100                                   | 95 to 100                                  |
| 1.18 mm                | 30 to 70                                  | 55 to 90                                   | 75 to 100                                   | 90 to 100                                  |
| 600 micron             | 15 to 34                                  | 35 to 59                                   | 60 to 79                                    | 80 to 100                                  |
| 300 micron             | 5 to 20                                   | 8 to 30                                    | 12 to 40                                    | 15 to 50                                   |
| 150 micron             | 0 to 10                                   | 0 to 10                                    | 0 to 10                                     | 0 to 15                                    |

- NOTE - 1 For crushed stone sands, the permissible Limit on 150 micron IS Sieve is increased to 20 percent. This does not affect the 5 percent allowance permitted in 4.5 applying to other sieve sizes.
- NOTE - 2 Fine Aggregate complying with the requirements of any grading zone in this table is suitable for concrete but the quality of concrete produced will depend upon a number of factors including proportions.
- NOTE - 3 Where concrete of high strength and good durability is required, fine aggregate conforming to any one of the four grading zones may be used, but the concrete mix should be properly

designed. As the fine aggregate grading becomes progressively finer, that is, from Grading Zones I to IV, the ratio of fine aggregate to coarse aggregate should be progressively reduced. The most suitable fine to coarse ratio to be used for any particular mix will, however, depend upon the actual grading, particle shape and surface texture of both fine and coarse aggregates.

NOTE - 4 It is recommended that fine aggregate conforming to Grading Zone IV should not be used in reinforced concrete unless tests have been made to ascertain the suitability of proposed mix proportions.

## PART 2 - PRODUCTS > 2.9 MISCELLANEOUS MATERIALS
- A. Cover blocks shall be of non-corrosive material such as plastic but not wooden or broken bricks or stone. High-density PVC chairs specifically made for this purpose shall be used in the Work. Concrete cover spaces may be permitted by the ER. Such concrete spacers shall be cast from concrete and not cement mortar. Strength of these blocks shall be at least equal to the strength of concrete in use. These should be fully cured prior to use in the Work.
- B. Binding wire shall be 16 or 18 gauge galvanized wire conforming to IS 280 . Binding shall be done with double wire. It shall be free from rust, oil, paint, grease, loose mill scale or any other deleterious material undesirable for the reinforcement and concrete or which may prevent adhesion of concrete with reinforcement.
- C. Deformed bars for concrete reinforcement and rolled mild steel and medium tensile steel conforming to IS 1139 shall be allowed in the Work provided they are approved by the ER.
- D. Grout: Free of gas-producing or gas-releasing agents, oxidizing catalysts, inorganic accelerators and chlorides. If requested by the ER, grout a sample (1.2m) x(1.2m) x (50mm) plate in the field and demonstrate a minimum of 95% bearing after curing 14 days. Cure grout in accordance with manufacturer's instructions.
- E. Vapor Barrier: Maximum (2.3 ng/Pa·s·m 2 ) water vapor permeance. Include manufacturer's recommended adhesive or pressure-sensitive joint tape. ASTM E1745, Class A or equal.
- F. Dustproofer and Chemical Hardener: Colorless, aqueous solution containing a blend of magnesium fluosilcate and zinc fluosilcate combined with a wetting agent, containing not less than (0.9kg/3.8L)of fluosilcate
- G. Waterstops: Self-Expanding Strip Waterstops: Flexible strip of bentonite (granular bentonite clay (sodium bentonite), minimum 85% montmorillonite (hydrated aluminum silicate), with a minimum 90% passing a (0.03mm) sieve) waterproofing compound in cartridge or coil form, designed specifically for vertical and horizontal joints in concrete construction.
